exposure: Residential solar ultraviolet (UV) light exposure at diagnosis
Residential solar ultraviolet (UV) light exposure at birth
Suspected individual risk factors for ALL (as confounders/effect modifiers)
outcome: Childhood precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PBC-ALL)
cohort: The study included 1,511 cases of leukemia aged less than 15 years and 3,102 population controls from the ESCALE (2003-2004) and ESTELLE (2010-2011) nationwide studies.
finding: The study found a positive association between residential UV radiation exposure at diagnosis (OR = 1.27 [1.08-1.48]) and childhood PBC-ALL, which remained consistent when considering exposure at birth and was not confounded or modified by individual risk factors.
cross-section timing: UV exposure was assessed at residence at birth and at residence at diagnosis/interview for cases (children aged less than 15 years at diagnosis) and controls.
